 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
     viewed from the right → highlight on the right                                                                                                                                     
     viewed from above     → highlight on top                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   A window:                                                                                                                                                                            
     viewed head-on        → transparent, you see through it                                                                                                                            
     viewed at an angle    → more reflective                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   These are NOT the same color at the same location.                                                                                                                                   
   The color depends on both WHERE you are and WHERE you're looking FROM.                                                                                                               
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 If you omit viewing direction, you can't represent reflections, specular highlights, or any glossy surface. The output looks flat and matte.                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### Why Is Density (σ) Separate From Color?                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Because density is a geometric property — it describes where matter is. It shouldn't change based on where you look from. A wall is equally solid whether you view it from the left or 
 the right.                                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Color does change with viewing direction. So:                                                                                                                                          
 - σ = F(x, y, z) — view-independent (same from all directions)                                                                                                                         
 - (r,g,b) = F(x, y, z, θ, φ) — view-dependent (changes with direction)                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The actual architecture enforces this: the MLP first processes (x,y,z) to get σ and an intermediate feature, then combines that feature with (θ, φ) to get color.                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Step 2 — The Neural Network Architecture                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 F is implemented as a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP). Here's the exact architecture from the paper:                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                   POSITIONAL           POSITIONAL                                                                                                                                      
                   ENCODING             ENCODING                                                                                                                                        
                   γ(x,y,z)             γ(θ,φ)                                                                                                                                          
                     │                    │                                                                                                                                             
                     ▼                    │                                                                                                                                             
                 [60-dim]                 │                                                                                                                                             
                     │                   │                                                                                                                                              
            ┌────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┐                                                                                                                           
            │                                               │                                                                                                                           
            │   Dense(256) → ReLU                           │                                                                                                                           
            │   Dense(256) → ReLU                           │                                                                                                                           
            │   Dense(256) → ReLU                           │                                                                                                                           
            │   Dense(256) → ReLU  ←── skip connection      │                                                                                                                           
            │         ↑                from input           │                                                                                                                           
            │   [concatenate γ(x,y,z) again here]           │                                                                                                                           
            │   Dense(256) → ReLU                           │                                                                                                                           
            │   Dense(256) → ReLU                           │                                                                                                                           
            │   Dense(256) → ReLU                           │                                                                                                                           
            │   Dense(256) → ReLU                           │                                                                                                                           
            │         │                                     │                                                                                                                           
            │         ├──→ Dense(1) → ReLU → σ (density)    │                                                                                                                           
            │         │                                     │                                                                                                                           
            │         ▼                                     │                                                                                                                           
            │   Dense(256) → feature vector                 │                                                                                                                           
            │         │                                     │                                                                                                                           
            │   [concatenate γ(θ,φ) here] ←────────────────┘                                                                                                                            
            │   Dense(128) → ReLU                                                                                                                                                       
            │   Dense(3)   → Sigmoid → (r, g, b)                                                                                                                                        
            └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘                                                                                                                            
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Key design decisions:                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ┌──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                                                                    
 │ Decision                     │ Reason                                                                           │                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                    
 │ ReLU activations             │ Standard, well-behaved gradients                                                 │                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                    
 │ Skip connection at layer 5   │ Prevents vanishing gradient in deep MLP; reminds network of original coordinates │                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                    
 │ Density before color         │ Geometry should be independent of view; color depends on geometry                │                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                    
 │ Sigmoid on color output      │ Keeps RGB in [0, 1]                                                              │                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                    
 │ ReLU on density output       │ Density must be non-negative                                                     │                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                    
 │ Positional encoding on input │ Fixes spectral bias — already explained in depth                                 │                                                                    
 └──────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is a tiny network by modern standards — ~1M parameters. The insight is that a single scene doesn't need a huge model. The scene's complexity is encoded in the weights, not the   
 architecture.                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Step 3 — Volume Rendering (The Differentiable Renderer)                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is the most mathematically beautiful part. We have F, a function that can answer "what color and density is at this 3D point?" Now we need to use that to render a 2D image.      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### Casting a Ray                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 For every pixel in the output image, we cast a ray from the camera origin o through that pixel into the scene:                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   r(t) = o + t·d                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   where:                                                                                                                                                                               
     o = camera position (origin of ray)                                                                                                                                                
     d = unit direction vector through the pixel                                                                                                                                        
     t = distance along the ray (the "depth")                                                                                                                                           
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Camera                                                                                                                                                                               
     📷  ───────────────────────────────────→  scene                                                                                                                                    
     o   t=0   t=1   t=2   t=3   t=4   t=5                                                                                                                                              
                 [air]  [air]  [wall]  [inside wall]                                                                                                                                    
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### The Volume Rendering Equation                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Now, what color does this ray produce? We query F at many points along the ray and composite the results. This comes from physics — specifically, from how light behaves when          
 traveling through a participating medium (fog, smoke, translucent materials).                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The classical volume rendering equation (from physics, 1960s):                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   C(r) = ∫[t_near to t_far]  T(t) · σ(r(t)) · c(r(t), d)  dt                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   where:                                                                                                                                                                               
     C(r)      = final rendered color of the ray                                                                                                                                        
     T(t)      = transmittance: how much light survives from t_near to t                                                                                                                
     σ(r(t))   = density at point r(t)   [from our NeRF]                                                                                                                                
     c(r(t),d) = color at point r(t)     [from our NeRF]                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   and:                                                                                                                                                                                 
     T(t) = exp( -∫[t_near to t] σ(r(s)) ds )                                                                                                                                           
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Intuition for transmittance T(t):                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   T(t) answers: "if a photon starts at t_near and travels to t, what fraction survives?"                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Dense material early → T drops to 0 quickly → back surfaces are occluded                                                                                                             
   Empty space         → T stays near 1      → light reaches far surfaces                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   T(t=0) = 1.0      (nothing blocks light at the start)                                                                                                                                
   T(t=5) = 0.001    (if there's a solid wall at t=3, almost no light gets past it)                                                                                                     
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### Discrete Approximation (What Actually Runs in Code)                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The integral becomes a sum over N sampled points:                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```python                                                                                                                                                                              
   def volume_render(colors, densities, deltas):                                                                                                                                        
       """                                                                                                                                                                              
       colors:    [N, 3]  — RGB at each sample point                                                                                                                                    
       densities: [N]     — σ at each sample point                                                                                                                                      
       deltas:    [N]     — distance between consecutive samples (δᵢ = tᵢ₊₁ - tᵢ)                                                                                                       
       """                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
       # Alpha: opacity of each thin slab                                                                                                                                               
       alphas = 1 - exp(-densities * deltas)         # αᵢ = 1 - e^(-σᵢδᵢ)                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
       # Transmittance: cumulative product of (1 - alpha) for all previous slabs                                                                                                        
       transmittance = cumprod(1 - alphas, exclusive=True)   # Tᵢ = ∏ⱼ<ᵢ (1 - αⱼ)                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
       # Weights: how much does each sample contribute to the final color?                                                                                                              
       weights = transmittance * alphas              # wᵢ = Tᵢ · αᵢ                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
       # Final color: weighted sum of sample colors                                                                                                                                     
       C = sum(weights * colors)                     # C = Σᵢ wᵢ · cᵢ                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
       return C                                                                                                                                                                         
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The weights wᵢ = Tᵢ · αᵢ are the key. Let's understand them:                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Sample point i gets high weight when:                                                                                                                                                
     ✅ Tᵢ is high  → nothing dense in front of it (it's visible)                                                                                                                       
     ✅ αᵢ is high  → it is itself dense (it's actual matter, not empty air)                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Sample point i gets zero weight when:                                                                                                                                                
     ❌ Tᵢ is low   → occluded by something in front of it                                                                                                                              
     ❌ αᵢ is low   → it's in empty space, nothing to see                                                                                                                               
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is exactly like attention weights in a Transformer:                                                                                                                               
 - Transmittance = "how much attention has already been used up"                                                                                                                        
 - Alpha = "how relevant is this position"                                                                                                                                              
 - The final output = weighted sum of values                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 In fact, NeRF's volume rendering is mathematically equivalent to sequential attention over depth, where each point "attends" to the final color output proportional to how visible and 
 dense it is.                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### Visualizing the Weights Along a Ray                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Example: Ray hitting a white wall behind a glass vase                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Depth:    0    1    2    3    4    5    6    7                                                                                                                                       
             [air][air][glass][glass][air][wall][wall]                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   σ:        0    0    0.5   0.5   0    10   10                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   T:        1.0  1.0  1.0   0.6   0.4  0.4  0.04                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   α:        0    0    0.4   0.4   0    1.0  1.0                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   weights:  0    0    0.4   0.24  0    0.36  0.04                                                                                                                                      
                       ↑glass↑     ↑wall↑                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Final color = 0.4 × (glass color) + 0.24 × (glass color) + 0.36 × (wall color) + ...                                                                                                 
               = mostly wall, partially visible through glass                                                                                                                           
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This naturally handles transparency, translucency, and partial occlusion — things that are hard with explicit meshes.                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Step 4 — Training                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### The Data                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Training data is simply: N photographs of a scene with known camera poses.                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Dataset:                                                                                                                                                                             
   ├── image_001.jpg  (camera pose: R₁, t₁)                                                                                                                                             
   ├── image_002.jpg  (camera pose: R₂, t₂)                                                                                                                                             
   ├── ...                                                                                                                                                                              
   └── image_100.jpg  (camera pose: R₁₀₀, t₁₀₀)                                                                                                                                         
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Camera poses come from COLMAP — a Structure from Motion (SfM) tool that estimates 3D camera positions by matching features across images. This is a prerequisite step, not part of     
 training.                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### The Loss Function                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Beautifully simple — just pixel-wise L2 loss between rendered and real colors:                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   L = (1/|R|) Σ_{r ∈ R} ||C_rendered(r) - C_real(r)||²                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   For every ray r in every training image:                                                                                                                                             
     1. Render the pixel color using volume rendering                                                                                                                                   
     2. Compare to the actual pixel color                                                                                                                                               
     3. Backpropagate through the volume renderer into the MLP weights                                                                                                                  
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 That's it. No 3D supervision. No depth maps. No segmentation masks. Just RGB images.                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 How does 3D structure emerge from this 2D loss?                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is the magic. The MLP is forced to be consistent across views. If a wall is at position (2, 3, 1), it must have high density there to correctly occlude things behind it in ALL   
 cameras simultaneously. There's only one assignment of (σ, color) to every 3D point that explains all views at once — and training finds it.                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 It's the same principle as how your two eyes give you depth perception: you infer 3D structure because you need to explain why the same object looks slightly different from each eye. 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### Hierarchical Sampling — The "Coarse to Fine" Trick                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Sampling points uniformly along a ray is wasteful. Most of the ray is empty space (σ ≈ 0), contributing nothing to the final color. You want to sample densely near surfaces.          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 NeRF solves this with two networks:                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Pass 1 — Coarse Network:                                                                                                                                                             
     Sample 64 points uniformly along the ray                                                                                                                                           
     Render the coarse color (and get weights wᵢ for each sample)                                                                                                                       
     The weights tell us WHERE density is concentrated                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Pass 2 — Fine Network:                                                                                                                                                               
     Use the coarse weights as a probability distribution                                                                                                                               
     Sample 128 MORE points, biased toward high-weight regions (near surfaces)                                                                                                          
     Render the fine color with all 64+128=192 points                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Loss = L_coarse + L_fine                                                                                                                                                             
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Uniform sampling:    · · · · · · · · · · · · · · · ·                                                                                                                                 
                                           ↑ wastes samples in empty space                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Hierarchical:        · · · · · ·····  · ·                                                                                                                                            
                                     ↑ concentrated near the surface                                                                                                                    
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is essentially importance sampling — a classic technique from Monte Carlo methods. You already know it from language model decoding (top-p sampling concentrates probability mass 
 where it matters).                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Step 5 — Putting It All Together                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Here's the full pipeline:                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   TRAINING:                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Photos + COLMAP poses                                                                                                                                                                
           │                                                                                                                                                                            
           ▼                                                                                                                                                                            
   For each training iteration:                                                                                                                                                         
     1. Sample a random ray (random image, random pixel)                                                                                                                                
     2. Sample 64 points along the ray (coarse)                                                                                                                                         
     3. Apply positional encoding to each point + direction                                                                                                                             
     4. Query coarse MLP → (σᵢ, cᵢ) for each point                                                                                                                                      
     5. Volume render → coarse color + sample weights                                                                                                                                   
     6. Sample 128 more points using weights (fine)                                                                                                                                     
     7. Query fine MLP → (σᵢ, cᵢ) for all 192 points                                                                                                                                    
     8. Volume render → fine color                                                                                                                                                      
     9. Loss = ||coarse - GT||² + ||fine - GT||²                                                                                                                                        
     10. Backprop → update MLP weights                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Repeat ~400,000 times (~24 hours on a V100)                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   INFERENCE (Novel View Synthesis):                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   New camera pose (R_new, t_new)                                                                                                                                                       
           │                                                                                                                                                                            
           ▼                                                                                                                                                                            
   For each pixel in the output image:                                                                                                                                                  
     1. Compute ray direction d from camera pose                                                                                                                                        
     2. Sample + encode + query fine MLP                                                                                                                                                
     3. Volume render → pixel color                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Repeat for all pixels → synthesized image                                                                                                                                            
   (~30 seconds per image)                                                                                                                                                              
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Step 6 — What Makes NeRF Work So Well                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Let's understand why this approach achieves results that were impossible before 2020.                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### 1. Continuous Representation = Infinite Resolution                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 A voxel grid at 512³ has fixed resolution — you can't zoom in beyond the voxel size. An MLP is a continuous function — you can query it at any precision. Want to render at 8K? Query  
 more points. The representation itself has no pixel budget.                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### 2. View-Dependent Effects for Free                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 By conditioning on viewing direction, NeRF handles reflections, specularity, and translucency naturally. Classical MVS (Multi-View Stereo) assumes all surfaces are Lambertian (matte) 
 and completely fails on shiny objects. NeRF does not make this assumption.                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### 3. No 3D Supervision Needed                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Training from RGB images only means you don't need:                                                                                                                                    
 - Expensive depth sensors                                                                                                                                                              
 - Manual 3D annotations                                                                                                                                                                
 - Perfect LIDAR scans                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Just a camera, some images, and COLMAP.                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### 4. The Representation is Implicit = No Topology Issues                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Meshes struggle with thin structures, holes, open surfaces. An implicit volumetric representation handles all of these — fog, hair, fire, tree leaves — as naturally as solid objects. 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The Weaknesses (and Why They Matter)                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 No honest explanation is complete without this:                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ┌────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                              
 │ Weakness                   │ Root Cause                                                      │ How Later Methods Fix It                               │                              
 ├────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                              
 │ Slow training (24h)        │ MLP queried millions of times per iteration, each query is slow │ Instant-NGP replaces MLP with hash table lookups       │                              
 ├────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                              
 │ Slow inference (30s/image) │ Must query MLP for 192 points × every pixel                     │ 3DGS uses rasterization (GPU-native, real-time)        │                              
 ├────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                              
 │ One model per scene        │ Weights encode one specific scene                               │ Generalizable NeRFs (pixelNeRF) add image conditioning │                              
 ├────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                              
 │ Needs ~100 images          │ Underdetermined with few views                                  │ RegNeRF, DietNeRF add regularization                   │                              
 ├────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                              
 │ Needs COLMAP poses         │ No pose estimation inside NeRF                                  │ BARF, NOPE-NeRF do joint pose+NeRF optimization        │                              
 ├────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                              
 │ Blurry on large scenes     │ Uniform sampling is inefficient at scale                        │ Mip-NeRF 360 adds scene contraction                    │                              
 ├────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                              
 │ Can't edit the scene       │ Weights are monolithic, no semantic structure                   │ Semantic NeRF, EditNeRF add disentanglement            │                              
 └────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Connecting Everything Back to NLP                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Since you come from NLP/LLMs, here's NeRF mapped to concepts you know:                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────┐                                                                                         
 │ NeRF Concept                               │ NLP Analogy                                   │                                                                                         
 ├────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                         
 │ The MLP = the scene                        │ The model weights = world knowledge           │                                                                                         
 ├────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                         
 │ Positional encoding γ(x,y,z)               │ Sinusoidal PE in Transformers                 │                                                                                         
 ├────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                         
 │ Volume rendering = weighted sum over depth │ Attention = weighted sum over sequence        │                                                                                         
 ├────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                         
 │ Transmittance T(t) = cumulative occlusion  │ Autoregressive mask = cumulative attention    │                                                                                         
 ├────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                         
 │ Training on pixels from all views          │ Training on tokens from all documents         │                                                                                         
 ├────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                         
 │ Overfitting one scene intentionally        │ Fine-tuning on one document corpus            │                                                                                         
 ├────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                         
 │ Hierarchical coarse-to-fine sampling       │ Speculative decoding / draft-then-verify      │                                                                                         
 ├────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                         
 │ σ(x) density = "is there content here?"    │ Token probability = "is this token relevant?" │                                                                                         
 ├────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                         
 │ One NeRF per scene                         │ One fine-tuned LLM per domain                 │                                                                                         
 └────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────┘                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The deepest analogy: a NeRF is to a 3D scene what a fine-tuned LLM is to a document corpus — a neural network that has memorized a specific world into its weights, and can answer     
 queries about it (render from new views / generate new text) by inference.                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Summary: NeRF in 6 Key Facts                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   1. WHAT IT IS:   A scene represented as a neural function (x,y,z,θ,φ) → (RGB, σ)                                                                                                     
                    implemented as an 8-layer MLP                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   2. HOW IT SEES:  Volume rendering — integrate colors along rays weighted by                                                                                                          
                    density and transmittance (like attention over depth)                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   3. HOW IT LEARNS: Pixel-wise L2 loss on rendered vs. real images, backprop                                                                                                           
                     through the differentiable volume renderer into MLP weights                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   4. KEY TRICK:    Positional encoding — pre-compute sinusoidal basis functions                                                                                                        
                    to overcome the MLP's spectral bias (same math as Transformer PE)                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   5. WHY IT WORKS: The scene's 3D structure must be consistent across all views                                                                                                        
                    simultaneously — the only explanation is correct geometry                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   6. WHY IT MATTERS: First method to achieve photorealistic novel view synthesis                                                                                                       
                      from just RGB images, without any 3D supervision                                                                                                                  
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Want to go to 3D Gaussian Splatting next? Understanding NeRF first makes 3DGS's design decisions feel inevitable — every part of 3DGS is a direct answer to one of NeRF's specific
