 ### Reason 2 — The MLP Has No Concept of Surfaces (Representation Problem)                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is more subtle and more fundamental. Consider what the MLP has to represent for a thin wire:                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Density along a ray passing through a 1mm wire:                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   σ(t):                                                                                                                                                                                
      │                                                                                                                                                                                 
   100│         ████                                                                                                                                                                    
      │        ██████                                                                                                                                                                   
      │       ████████                                                                                                                                                                  
     0│───────────────────── t (depth)                                                                                                                                                  
          ↑ sharp spike, 1mm wide                                                                                                                                                       
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is a high-frequency function in the spatial domain — a sharp spike. Recall the spectral bias discussion: MLPs are biased toward smooth, low-frequency functions. Even with        
 positional encoding providing high-frequency basis functions, the combination of those basis functions into a sharp spike requires extremely precise coefficient tuning.               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 More precisely: at any given 3D location, the positional encoding provides the potential to represent high-frequency content. But learning to place a sharp density spike in exactly   
 the right location, with the right width, from 2D image supervision alone, is hard. The MLP tends to represent the wire as a diffuse cloud of density — low density spread over a      
 wider region — rather than a sharp concentrated peak.                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The result looks like a blurry halo where the wire should be, instead of a sharp wire.                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Compare to what 3DGS does: each Gaussian has an explicit size (the scale parameter s). To represent a thin wire, you'd ideally want Gaussians with very small scale in two dimensions  
 and larger scale along the wire's length — thin, elongated ellipsoids placed along the wire. The explicit shape representation should make this easier.                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 But 3DGS still struggles — for a different reason we'll get to in a moment.                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Reason 3 — Multi-View Consistency Is Impossible to Satisfy (Supervision Problem)                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is the deepest reason. Consider a thin wire seen from different camera angles:                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Camera angle 0°:                   Camera angle 45°:                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
      ─────────────────                  ─────────────────                                                                                                                              
              |||                               /                                                                                                                                       
              |||  ← wire appears              /  ← wire appears                                                                                                                        
              |||    clearly as               /     thinner, maybe                                                                                                                      
            width   a column               width   1 pixel wide                                                                                                                         
              |||                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Camera angle 90° (end-on):                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
      ─────────────────                                                                                                                                                                 
              ·                                                                                                                                                                         
              ·  ← wire appears as                                                                                                                                                      
              ·     a dot, ~0 width                                                                                                                                                     
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The wire's image-space footprint varies from "a few pixels wide" to "literally one pixel" to "sub-pixel" depending on viewing angle. Now NeRF must learn a single 3D density function  
 that is consistent with all these views simultaneously.                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The loss pushes the network in contradictory directions:                                                                                                                               
 - From the head-on view: "put high density here in this column"                                                                                                                        
 - From the 90° view: "there's almost nothing at that location"                                                                                                                         
 - From 45°: "somewhere in between"                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The only 3D density function that explains all views perfectly is an infinitely thin spike — which is:                                                                                 
 1. Not representable by an MLP (infinite frequency)                                                                                                                                    
 2. Practically unsamplable (measure zero)                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The network compromises with a volumetric blob — something that looks vaguely right from every angle but perfectly right from none. The wire renders as a fuzzy column of low density. 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is sometimes called the "needle in a volume" problem — thin, elongated structures that are fundamentally incompatible with continuous volumetric representations.                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Why 3DGS Also Struggles (Just Differently)                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 You might think: "OK, but 3DGS uses explicit Gaussians with controllable size — couldn't it just use thin elongated Gaussians?"                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 In theory yes. In practice, three problems:                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### Problem A — The Sorting Ambiguity                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 For a thin wire, you need several overlapping elongated Gaussians placed along the wire. When the camera looks at them nearly end-on, these Gaussians are at nearly the same depth.    
 The depth sort becomes ambiguous — tiny changes in camera position flip the sort order, causing the wire to flicker.                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### Problem B — ADC Doesn't Know to Use Elongated Gaussians                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The adaptive density control creates and splits Gaussians based on gradient magnitude. For a thin wire, it tends to scatter many small spherical Gaussians around the wire rather than 
 creating a few long thin ones aligned with it. The optimization landscape is flat with respect to aligning the Gaussian axes with the wire — rotating a small sphere doesn't change    
 the loss much.                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### Problem C — The Same Multi-View Supervision Problem                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The supervision problem from Reason 3 above is not specific to NeRF. 3DGS faces the exact same issue: the image-space footprint of a thin Gaussian changes dramatically with viewing   
 angle, and the loss from all views simultaneously is hard to satisfy with any explicit primitive.                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The Research Attempts to Fix Both                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ┌────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                    
 │ Method                         │ Approach                                                   │ Addresses                                                         │                    
 ├────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                    
 │ RegNeRF (2022)                 │ Regularization on unseen views to force coherent geometry  │ NeRF multi-view inconsistency                                     │                    
 ├────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                    
 │ NeuS (2021)                    │ Replace NeRF's density with Signed Distance Function (SDF) │ NeRF's blob geometry — SDF has a well-defined surface             │                    
 ├────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                    
 │ VolSDF (2021)                  │ Similar to NeuS, density derived from SDF                  │ Same                                                              │                    
 ├────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                    
 │ 2DGS (2024)                    │ Replace 3D Gaussians with 2D flat disks                    │ 3DGS thin structure problem — disks align with surfaces naturally │                    
 ├────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                    
 │ Gaussian Opacity Fields (2024) │ Extract SDF from 3DGS                                      │ 3DGS geometry quality                                             │                    
 └────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 NeuS is worth noting here — it's an important bridge method. Instead of arbitrary volume density σ, NeuS parameterizes the scene as a Signed Distance Function: a value that is 0      
 exactly at the surface, positive outside, negative inside. This gives you a well-defined, mathematically exact surface — no blobs, no diffuse clouds. Thin objects are representable   
 as long as their SDF can be computed. Quality-wise NeuS is below 3DGS, but its geometry is far more accurate.                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 2DGS is the cleanest solution for 3DGS: instead of a 3D ellipsoid, each primitive is a flat 2D disk (a "splat" in 2 dimensions). Disks naturally align with surfaces, their            
 cross-section doesn't change as dramatically with viewing angle, and thin structures can be represented by edge-on disks.                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Summary                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ┌────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ 
 │ Problem                │ NeRF Root Cause                                                   │ 3DGS Root Cause                                                                       │ 
 ├────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ 
 │ Thin objects blurry    │ Sampler misses thin regions; MLP can't represent sharp density    │ ADC doesn't create thin Gaussians; optimization doesn't align them                    │ 
 │                        │ spikes                                                            │                                                                                       │ 
 ├────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ 
 │ Sharp highlights wrong │ N/A (MLP handles view-dependence freely)                          │ Degree-3 SH can't represent sub-60° angular variation                                 │ 
 ├────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ 
 │ Shared root            │ —                                                                 │ Both stem from representing high-frequency structure with limited-bandwidth           │ 
 │                        │                                                                   │ approximations                                                                        │ 
 └────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The pattern across both problems is the same one from the spectral bias discussion — high-frequency structure is always the hard part, whether that frequency is in spatial density    
 (thin objects) or angular color variation (sharp highlights). Every limitation in neural rendering traces back to this fundamental tension.                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Ready to move on to COLMAP, 4DGS, or start the code?                                                                                                                                   

                                                                                                                                                                                        
 4DGS                                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        

 The user wants to learn about 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS). Let me give a comprehensive explanation building on their understanding of 3DGS, covering:                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 1. The problem - why 3DGS fails for dynamic scenes                                                                                                                                     
 2. The conceptual approaches to adding time                                                                                                                                            
 3. The main 4DGS methods (there are multiple independent works)                                                                                                                        
 4. The math - 4D Gaussians, deformation fields, etc.                                                                                                                                   
 5. Training and rendering                                                                                                                                                              
 6. Connections to their NLP background                                                                                                                                                 
 7. Current SOTA and limitations                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 There are several key papers:                                                                                                                                                          
 1. 4D Gaussian Splatting (Wu et al., 2023) - "4D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Dynamic Scene Rendering" - CVPR 2024                                                                 
 2. Deformable 3D Gaussians (Yang et al., 2023) - "Deformable 3D Gaussians for High-Fidelity Monocular Dynamic Scene Reconstruction"                                                    
 3. Real-time 4D Gaussian Splatting (Yang et al., 2023) - a different paper by different authors                                                                                        
 4. Spacetime Gaussians (Li et al., 2023) - "Spacetime Gaussian Feature Splatting for Real-Time Dynamic View Synthesis"                                                                 
 5. 4DGaussians (Duan et al., 2023)                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 These represent the main competing approaches that emerged around the same time, each with slightly different strategies for handling temporal dynamics.                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The fundamental issue is that 3DGS works for static scenes, but once objects or the camera move, the fixed Gaussians can't capture that motion. The solutions split into two main      
 camps: one uses a deformation field that learns how each Gaussian shifts over time through an MLP, similar to how D-NeRF handles dynamic NeRFs. The other extends Gaussians into 4D    
 space-time, where marginalizing over the temporal dimension gives you the 3D representation at any moment.                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 A third approach uses polynomial time coefficients for position and rotation—treating motion like kinematics with position evolving as μ₀ + v·t + a·t²—which is more interpretable and 
 computationally efficient. I should walk through all three with enough detail to show how they handle the temporal dimension, explain the canonical space concept and deformation      
 fields, cover 4D covariance and marginalization, discuss temporal basis functions, and address how training works with video data, especially since we have multi-camera footage which 
 is ideal for this.                                                                                                                                                                     

 4D Gaussian Splatting                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Let's build this the right way — starting from exactly where 3DGS breaks down, then deriving the three main approaches the field took, understanding why each makes the choices it     
 does.                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The Core Problem: Time Breaks Everything                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 3DGS makes one silent assumption that the entire method depends on:                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 │ The scene is static.                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Every design decision — the Gaussian positions, the depth sort, the training loss — assumes that what's true at frame 1 is true at frame 1000. The Gaussians are fixed in space. There 
 is no concept of time in the representation.                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Now introduce motion. A person waves their hand. A flag flaps in the wind. A car drives past.                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Frame 0:        Frame 15:       Frame 30:                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
     o              o               o                                                                                                                                                   
    /|\            /|              /|\                                                                                                                                                  
    / \           / \             /   \                                                                                                                                                 
   (hand left)  (hand center)  (hand right)                                                                                                                                             
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 What happens if you naively train a static 3DGS on all frames of this video?                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   The Gaussians see contradictory supervision:                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
     Training image at t=0:  "hand is on the LEFT"                                                                                                                                      
     Training image at t=15: "hand is in the CENTER"                                                                                                                                    
     Training image at t=30: "hand is on the RIGHT"                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   The only way to explain all three simultaneously with static Gaussians:                                                                                                              
     → Spread density across all three positions                                                                                                                                        
     → Low opacity everywhere (ghosting)                                                                                                                                                
     → Result: blurry smear where the hand should be                                                                                                                                    
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is called motion blur artifacts — the model time-averages the motion rather than representing it.                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The fundamental question 4DGS must answer:                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 │ How do you represent a scene that changes over time?                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 There are three distinct philosophical answers the field converged on simultaneously in late 2023. Let's understand each.                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The Three Approaches                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   How do you handle time in 3DGS?                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Approach 1:  DEFORMATION FIELD                                                                                                                                                       
                One canonical set of Gaussians + a function that says                                                                                                                   
                "at time t, move each Gaussian by this much"                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Approach 2:  TRUE 4D GAUSSIANS                                                                                                                                                       
                Extend Gaussians to 4 dimensions (x, y, z, t)                                                                                                                           
                Time is just another spatial dimension with its own covariance                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Approach 3:  EXPLICIT MOTION COEFFICIENTS                                                                                                                                            
                Give each Gaussian its own polynomial trajectory                                                                                                                        
                Position is a function of time, encoded as coefficients                                                                                                                 
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 These are not just implementation details — they represent fundamentally different beliefs about how scenes work.                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Approach 1 — Deformable 3D Gaussians                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Paper: "Deformable 3D Gaussians for High-Fidelity Monocular Dynamic Scene Reconstruction" — Yang et al., 2023                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The Intuition: Canonical Space + Deformation                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is the most intuitive approach, directly inspired by how animators work. In 3D animation, you have:                                                                               
 - A rest pose (the character in a neutral position, T-pose)                                                                                                                            
 - A rig (a function that deforms the rest pose into any other pose)                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Deformable 3DGS does exactly this:                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   CANONICAL SPACE:           OBSERVATION SPACE:                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Static Gaussians           Deformed Gaussians at time t                                                                                                                              
   G = {μᵢ, Rᵢ, Sᵢ, αᵢ, SHᵢ}    G(t) = {μᵢ + Δμᵢ(t), Rᵢ·ΔRᵢ(t), Sᵢ·ΔSᵢ(t), αᵢ, SHᵢ}                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
            ──────── Deformation Network f_θ(μᵢ, t) ────────→                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
                              (Δμ, ΔR, ΔS) per Gaussian per timestep                                                                                                                    
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The canonical Gaussians are the "rest pose" of the scene — what it looks like at some reference state. The deformation network maps each Gaussian + time → the offset from that rest   
 pose.                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The Deformation Network Architecture                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```python                                                                                                                                                                              
   def deformation_network(mu_canonical, time_t):                                                                                                                                       
       """                                                                                                                                                                              
       mu_canonical: [N, 3] — canonical positions of all Gaussians                                                                                                                      
       time_t:       scalar — normalized timestamp ∈ [0, 1]                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                        
       Returns:                                                                                                                                                                         
       delta_mu:   [N, 3] — position offsets                                                                                                                                            
       delta_rot:  [N, 4] — rotation offsets (quaternion)                                                                                                                               
       delta_scale:[N, 3] — scale offsets                                                                                                                                               
       """                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
       # Encode time with positional encoding (same as NeRF!)                                                                                                                           
       t_encoded = positional_encoding(time_t, L=6)   # 12-dim                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
       # Encode canonical position                                                                                                                                                      
       mu_encoded = positional_encoding(mu_canonical, L=10)  # 60-dim                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
       # Concatenate and pass through small MLP                                                                                                                                         
       features = MLP([mu_encoded, t_encoded])   # 6 layers, 256 units                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
       delta_mu    = Linear(features, 3)                                                                                                                                                
       delta_rot   = Linear(features, 4)   # quaternion offset                                                                                                                          
       delta_scale = Linear(features, 3)                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
       return delta_mu, delta_rot, delta_scale                                                                                                                                          
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Note: positional encoding on time — again the same spectral bias fix. Time has high-frequency structure (fast motion needs high-frequency temporal representation).                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The Rendering Pipeline                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   For each training frame at time t:                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   1. Query deformation network: f_θ(μᵢ, t) → (Δμᵢ, ΔRᵢ, ΔSᵢ) for all Gaussians                                                                                                         
   2. Apply deformation:                                                                                                                                                                
          μᵢ(t)  = μᵢ + Δμᵢ                                                                                                                                                             
          Rᵢ(t)  = Rᵢ · ΔRᵢ                                                                                                                                                             
          Sᵢ(t)  = Sᵢ ⊙ exp(ΔSᵢ)                                                                                                                                                        
   3. Render deformed Gaussians with standard 3DGS pipeline                                                                                                                             
   4. Loss vs. GT frame at time t                                                                                                                                                       
   5. Backprop through renderer → through deformation network → update both                                                                                                             
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The canonical Gaussians and the deformation network are trained jointly.                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### What the Deformation Network Learns                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Visualize what f_θ is actually encoding:                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Gaussian on the tip of a waving hand:                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   t=0.0:  Δμ = [-0.3, 0.0, 0.0]   ← hand is left                                                                                                                                       
   t=0.25: Δμ = [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]   ← hand is center (this is the canonical pose)                                                                                                        
   t=0.5:  Δμ = [+0.3, 0.0, 0.0]   ← hand is right                                                                                                                                      
   t=0.75: Δμ = [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]   ← hand is center again                                                                                                                               
   t=1.0:  Δμ = [-0.3, 0.0, 0.0]   ← hand is left again                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   The network learns: this Gaussian oscillates sinusoidally in x with period T                                                                                                         
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Rigid objects → Δμ varies, ΔR and ΔS stay near zero                                                                                                                                    
 Deforming objects (cloth, skin) → all three vary                                                                                                                                       
 Background → Δμ ≈ 0 everywhere (static)                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Strengths and Weaknesses                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                                                    
 │ ✅ Strengths                                    │ ❌ Weaknesses                                                                 │                                                    
 ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                    
 │ Interpretable — canonical space is visualizable │ MLP for deformation reintroduces spectral bias                                │                                                    
 ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                    
 │ Elegant factorization: geometry vs. motion      │ Assumes topology doesn't change (can't handle objects appearing/disappearing) │                                                    
 ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                    
 │ Canonical space can be edited                   │ Slow for large scenes (N queries through MLP per frame)                       │                                                    
 ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                    
 │ Works with monocular video                      │ Canonical space choice is ambiguous                                           │                                                    
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The Topology Problem                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The most fundamental limitation: deformation assumes the same set of Gaussians exist at all timesteps, just in different positions. What if:                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   A person walks into frame at t=50?    → New Gaussians needed that didn't exist before                                                                                                
   A ball explodes?                      → Gaussians need to split in ways ADC can't handle                                                                                             
   Two objects merge?                    → Topology changes                                                                                                                             
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Deformable 3DGS cannot handle these cases. The canonical set is fixed at initialization.                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Approach 2 — True 4D Gaussian Splatting                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Paper: "4D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Dynamic Scene Rendering" — Wu et al., 2023 (CVPR 2024)                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The Conceptual Leap                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 What if time isn't a special "external" variable that drives a deformation network, but just another dimension of the Gaussian itself?                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 In 3DGS, a Gaussian is a distribution over 3D space:                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   G₃D(x) = exp(-½ (x - μ)ᵀ Σ₃D⁻¹ (x - μ))                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   where x = (x, y, z)                                                                                                                                                                  
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 In 4DGS, a Gaussian is a distribution over 4D spacetime:                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   G₄D(x, t) = exp(-½ [x-μ, t-τ]ᵀ Σ₄D⁻¹ [x-μ, t-τ])                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   where [x, t] = (x, y, z, t)                                                                                                                                                          
         μ = (μₓ, μᵧ, μᵤ) — spatial center                                                                                                                                              
         τ = temporal center                                                                                                                                                            
         Σ₄D = 4×4 covariance matrix encoding spatial shape AND temporal extent                                                                                                         
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is not just a notational trick. The 4D covariance Σ₄D encodes:                                                                                                                    
 - Spatial shape — how big and what orientation in 3D space                                                                                                                             
 - Temporal extent — how long this Gaussian "lives"                                                                                                                                     
 - Spacetime correlation — how the spatial shape changes with time                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 That last point is the key. Let's understand it.                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The 4D Covariance and What It Encodes                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 A 4×4 covariance matrix has this block structure:                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Σ₄D = | Σ_xx   Σ_xt |                                                                                                                                                                
         | Σ_tx   Σ_tt |                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   where:                                                                                                                                                                               
     Σ_xx (3×3) = spatial covariance (same as 3DGS Σ₃D)                                                                                                                                 
     Σ_tt (1×1) = temporal variance (how long the Gaussian lasts)                                                                                                                       
     Σ_xt (3×1) = spacetime cross-covariance ← THE NEW THING                                                                                                                            
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The cross-covariance Σ_xt encodes how spatial position is correlated with time — in other words, velocity and acceleration.                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Intuitively:                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Σ_xt = 0:          Σ_xt ≠ 0:                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
     t                   t                                                                                                                                                              
     │  ●●●●●            │     ●●●●●                                                                                                                                                    
     │  ●●●●●            │   ●●●●●                                                                                                                                                      
     │  ●●●●●            │  ●●●●●                                                                                                                                                       
     └──────── x         └──────── x                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
     Gaussian doesn't      Gaussian moves in x                                                                                                                                          
     move over time        as time progresses                                                                                                                                           
     (static object)       (moving object)                                                                                                                                              
 ```
