 A non-zero Σ_xt literally encodes that the Gaussian's position in x,y,z drifts linearly with time. This is velocity built directly into the covariance structure.                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Marginalizing to Get a 3D Gaussian at Time t                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 To render at a specific timestep t*, you need a 3D Gaussian. You get it by marginalizing the 4D Gaussian over time — conditioning on t = t*:                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   G₄D(x, t) marginalized at t = t*:                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   G₃D(x | t=t*) is a 3D Gaussian with:                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
     μ(t*) = μ_spatial + Σ_xt · Σ_tt⁻¹ · (t* - τ)                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
     Σ(t*) = Σ_xx - Σ_xt · Σ_tt⁻¹ · Σ_tx                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   This is the standard formula for conditioning a multivariate Gaussian.                                                                                                               
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The adjusted mean μ(t*) is the original position plus a time-dependent offset — the Gaussian has moved. The adjusted covariance Σ(t*) is the original covariance minus a term — the    
 Gaussian's shape has changed (become more certain in the conditioned direction).                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is exactly the conditional Gaussian formula from basic probability:                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   If (X, Y) ~ N(μ, Σ), then:                                                                                                                                                           
   X | Y = y  ~  N(μ_x + Σ_xy Σ_yy⁻¹(y - μ_y),   Σ_xx - Σ_xy Σ_yy⁻¹ Σ_yx)                                                                                                               
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 You already know this if you've worked with Gaussian processes — which are used in Bayesian hyperparameter optimization, something NLP folks encounter in tuning LLMs.                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The Full 4DGS Representation                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Each 4D Gaussian stores:                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   μ   ∈ ℝ³    — spatial center                                                                                                                                                         
   τ   ∈ ℝ     — temporal center ("when does this Gaussian peak?")                                                                                                                      
   Σ₄D ∈ ℝ^4×4 — 4D covariance (decomposed for optimization)                                                                                                                            
   α   ∈ [0,1] — opacity                                                                                                                                                                
   SH  ∈ ℝ^48  — spherical harmonics for color                                                                                                                                          
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 And the 4D covariance is decomposed as:                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Σ₄D = L L ᵀ    (Cholesky decomposition — ensures positive semi-definiteness)                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   L = | L_xx   0  |     (lower triangular block form)                                                                                                                                  
       | l_tx   l_tt|                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Parameters: 6 (for L_xx) + 3 (for l_tx) + 1 (for l_tt) = 10 parameters                                                                                                               
   vs. 3DGS: 7 parameters for Σ₃D                                                                                                                                                       
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 3 extra parameters per Gaussian encode all of the temporal behavior.                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Why This Is Elegant                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The 4D Gaussian approach achieves something beautiful: there is no separate motion model. Time is not an external input to a deformation function. The Gaussian is the motion. The     
 math of multivariate Gaussians handles everything:                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 - Static object: Σ_xt = 0 → conditioning on t doesn't change the mean                                                                                                                  
 - Linear motion: Σ_xt ≠ 0 → the mean shifts linearly with t (constant velocity)                                                                                                        
 - Short-lived event: Σ_tt is small → Gaussian has narrow temporal support (disappears quickly)                                                                                         
 - Persistent feature: Σ_tt is large → Gaussian spans many frames                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The temporal extent Σ_tt also handles object appearance and disappearance — something Approach 1 cannot do. A Gaussian with small Σ_tt effectively only exists for a few frames.       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Rendering                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   For timestep t*:                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   1. For each 4D Gaussian:                                                                                                                                                             
      a. Compute μ(t*) and Σ(t*) via conditioning formula                                                                                                                               
      b. Compute temporal weight: w(t*) = exp(-½(t* - τ)²/Σ_tt)                                                                                                                         
         (how "active" is this Gaussian at this time?)                                                                                                                                  
      c. Effective opacity: α_eff = α · w(t*)                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   2. Project resulting 3D Gaussians to screen                                                                                                                                          
   3. Standard 3DGS rasterization                                                                                                                                                       
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The temporal weight w(t*) is key: Gaussians whose temporal center τ is far from t* have low weight → they contribute little to the rendering. This naturally handles the scene         
 changing over time.                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Weakness: Only Linear Motion                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The 4D Gaussian formulation can only represent linear motion (constant velocity) directly — because the conditioning formula gives a linear shift in the mean with t. Non-linear       
 motion (acceleration, oscillation) requires many overlapping Gaussians covering different time windows, each linear locally. This works but is inefficient and blurry for fast complex 
 motions.                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Approach 3 — Spacetime Gaussians (Explicit Motion Coefficients)                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Paper: "Spacetime Gaussian Feature Splatting for Real-Time Dynamic View Synthesis" — Li et al., CVPR 2024                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The Idea: Physics-Inspired Trajectories                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Instead of a deformation network or 4D covariance, give each Gaussian its own polynomial trajectory in time:                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Gaussian position at time t:                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   μ(t) = μ₀ + v·t + ½a·t²                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   where:                                                                                                                                                                               
     μ₀ = initial position  (3 params)                                                                                                                                                  
     v  = velocity          (3 params)                                                                                                                                                  
     a  = acceleration      (3 params)                                                                                                                                                  
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is literally Newton's kinematic equations. Similarly for rotation:                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Rotation at time t:  q(t) = q₀ + ω·t                                                                                                                                                 
   Scale at time t:     s(t) = s₀ + ṡ·t                                                                                                                                                 
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 So each Gaussian now stores its full kinematic state:                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   μ₀, v, a    — position trajectory (9 params)                                                                                                                                         
   q₀, ω       — rotation trajectory (7 params)                                                                                                                                         
   s₀, ṡ       — scale trajectory    (6 params)                                                                                                                                         
   α(t)        — time-varying opacity (parameterized as a small MLP or polynomial)                                                                                                      
   SH          — color (same as 3DGS)                                                                                                                                                   
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Total: ~30 extra parameters per Gaussian vs. 3DGS's 59. So roughly 90 parameters per Gaussian.                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Why Polynomials?                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Three reasons:                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 1. Efficient evaluation: Given t, computing μ(t) = μ₀ + v·t + ½a·t² is 6 multiplications and 6 additions. No network forward pass.                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 2. Physically meaningful: Real objects follow smooth trajectories. Polynomial approximation is good for short time windows.                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 3. Differentiable with respect to everything: Gradients flow from pixel error → Gaussian position at time t → μ₀, v, a directly. No MLP Jacobians to compute.                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Temporal Basis Functions (The Generalization)                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The full Spacetime Gaussians paper generalizes beyond polynomials. Each Gaussian's trajectory is:                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   μ(t) = Σₖ cₖ · φₖ(t)                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   where φₖ(t) are temporal basis functions (e.g., polynomials, B-splines, or Fourier modes)                                                                                            
   and cₖ are learned coefficients                                                                                                                                                      
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is exactly analogous to positional encoding — you choose a set of basis functions that span the temporal frequencies you expect in the scene, and learn coefficients for each     
 Gaussian.                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 For a scene with mostly slow motion, degree-2 polynomials are enough. For fast oscillatory motion (vibrating string), you'd use Fourier modes.                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Opacity Over Time                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 One critical innovation: time-varying opacity. This is what handles objects entering/leaving the frame, or partial occlusion changes:                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```python                                                                                                                                                                              
   def opacity_at_time(t, alpha_0, alpha_params):                                                                                                                                       
       # Small polynomial or learned function for opacity trajectory                                                                                                                    
       # alpha_0: base opacity                                                                                                                                                          
       # alpha_params: time-varying component                                                                                                                                           
       return sigmoid(alpha_0 + alpha_params[0]*t + alpha_params[1]*t²)                                                                                                                 
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 A Gaussian can "fade in" as an object enters the scene and "fade out" as it leaves — something that pure deformation cannot achieve.                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Comparison of the Three Approaches                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ┌──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┐                                                       
 │                      │ Deformable 3DGS              │ 4D Gaussians                     │ Spacetime Gaussians                 │                                                       
 ├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤                                                       
 │ Motion model         │ MLP deformation field        │ 4D covariance conditioning       │ Polynomial trajectory               │                                                       
 ├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤                                                       
 │ Speed                │ Slow (MLP query per frame)   │ Fast (closed form)               │ Fastest (arithmetic only)           │                                                       
 ├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤                                                       
 │ Non-linear motion    │ Yes (MLP can learn anything) │ Approximate (multiple Gaussians) │ Limited by polynomial degree        │                                                       
 ├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤                                                       
 │ Topology change      │ ❌ No                        │ ✅ Partial (via temporal extent) │ ✅ Partial (via opacity trajectory) │                                                       
 ├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤                                                       
 │ Interpretability     │ Moderate (canonical space)   │ High (explicit covariance)       │ Highest (explicit kinematics)       │                                                       
 ├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤                                                       
 │ Training data needed │ Multi-view or monocular      │ Ideally multi-view               │ Multi-view preferred                │                                                       
 ├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤                                                       
 │ Memory               │ Low extra (+MLP weights)     │ Low extra (+3 params)            │ Moderate extra (+~30 params)        │                                                       
 └──────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────┘                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The Training Setup — Where Our Dataset Shines                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Here's where the multi-camera video dataset you found becomes important. There are two distinct training regimes:                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### Monocular Dynamic NeRF/3DGS — The Hard Problem                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Setup:  ONE camera records a dynamic scene                                                                                                                                           
           (like a single phone camera filming someone dancing)                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   What you observe:                                                                                                                                                                    
     Frame 0: [image from camera A at t=0]                                                                                                                                              
     Frame 1: [image from camera A at t=1]                                                                                                                                              
     Frame 2: [image from camera A at t=2]                                                                                                                                              
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Why this is hard: At each timestep, you only have ONE view. One view is nowhere near enough to determine 3D structure — the fundamental ambiguity of depth from a single image. You    
 must use temporal consistency as a proxy for 3D consistency — assuming that what was visible at t=0 should smoothly connect to t=1. This is a weak constraint and leads to significant 
 reconstruction artifacts.                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is like asking someone to reconstruct a 3D sculpture by watching it from one fixed angle as it rotates — you can infer some things, but there are always ambiguous cases.         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 #### Multi-View Dynamic — What We Have                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Setup:  N synchronized cameras record the same dynamic scene                                                                                                                         
           (our dataset: multiple cameras, same scene, same timestep)                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   What you observe:                                                                                                                                                                    
     Frame 0: [image from camera 1 at t=0]                                                                                                                                              
              [image from camera 2 at t=0]                                                                                                                                              
              [image from camera 3 at t=0]                                                                                                                                              
              ...                                                                                                                                                                       
     Frame 1: [image from camera 1 at t=1]                                                                                                                                              
              [image from camera 2 at t=1]                                                                                                                                              
              ...                                                                                                                                                                       
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Why this is much better: At each timestep, you have N views simultaneously. This is enough to determine 3D structure via standard triangulation — the same math as stereo vision. The  
 dynamic problem becomes:                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Static 3DGS per timestep + temporal consistency constraint                                                                                                                           
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Instead of fighting the underdetermination of monocular reconstruction, you have a well-posed 3D problem at each instant, connected across time.                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is precisely the regime where 4DGS methods work best and produce their published results.                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The Full 4DGS Training Pipeline (What We'll Actually Run)                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Using the Deformable 3DGS approach as a concrete example (most stable codebase):                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   PHASE 1: Initialization (same as static 3DGS)                                                                                                                                        
   ─────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                                                        
   1. Run COLMAP on all cameras at t=0 (reference frame)                                                                                                                                
      → Camera poses for all N cameras                                                                                                                                                  
      → Sparse point cloud for Gaussian initialization                                                                                                                                  
   2. Initialize canonical Gaussians from point cloud                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   PHASE 2: Warm-Up Training (static)                                                                                                                                                   
   ────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                                                                 
   Iterations 1-3000:                                                                                                                                                                   
     Train only on t=0 frames with ZERO deformation                                                                                                                                     
     (Δμ = 0, ΔR = I, ΔS = 1)                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
     Purpose: Get canonical Gaussians into a reasonable configuration                                                                                                                   
              before the deformation network starts contributing noise                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   PHASE 3: Joint Training (dynamic)                                                                                                                                                    
   ───────────────────────────────────                                                                                                                                                  
   Iterations 3000-30000:                                                                                                                                                               
     For each iteration:                                                                                                                                                                
       1. Sample random timestep t*                                                                                                                                                     
       2. Sample random camera at t*                                                                                                                                                    
       3. Query deformation network: Δ = f_θ(μ_canonical, t*)                                                                                                                           
       4. Apply deformation: G(t*) = G_canonical + Δ                                                                                                                                    
       5. Render with standard 3DGS rasterizer                                                                                                                                          
       6. Loss = L₁ + λ·L_SSIM                                                                                                                                                          
       7. + Regularization losses:                                                                                                                                                      
             L_rigid   = penalty for non-rigid deformations near neighbors                                                                                                              
             L_rotation = penalty for large rotations (keeps motion smooth)                                                                                                             
             L_isometry = nearby Gaussians should stay nearby (preserve local structure)                                                                                                
       8. Backprop → update canonical Gaussians AND deformation network                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   PHASE 4: ADC (Adaptive Density Control)                                                                                                                                              
   ─────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                                                            
   Same as static 3DGS but applied to canonical Gaussians                                                                                                                               
   Prune/clone based on gradients averaged across all timesteps                                                                                                                         
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The Regularization Losses — Why They're Needed                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Without extra constraints, the deformation network will find degenerate solutions:                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Degenerate solution 1: "Teleporting Gaussians"                                                                                                                                       
     At t=0: Gaussian G₁ explains the nose                                                                                                                                              
     At t=1: G₁ has Δμ = [10, 5, 3] → teleports to explain the ear                                                                                                                      
     At t=0 again (other frame): G₁ teleports back                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
     Loss is low! But the "deformation" is physically meaningless.                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Degenerate solution 2: "Transparency cheating"                                                                                                                                       
     Instead of moving Gaussians, set α → 0 at t where the object moved                                                                                                                 
     A new set of Gaussians at α > 0 at the new position                                                                                                                                
     Effectively has two "copies" of every object, one active at a time.                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
     Again, loss is low but representation is garbage.                                                                                                                                  
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Regularization losses prevent these:                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   L_rigid:    Neighboring Gaussians should have similar deformations                                                                                                                   
               (rigid body motion = all parts move together)                                                                                                                            
               Prevents teleporting of individual Gaussians                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   L_rotation: Deformation rotations should be small                                                                                                                                    
               (no wild spinning)                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   L_isometry: Distance between Gaussians should be preserved                                                                                                                           
               (elastic, not plastic deformation)                                                                                                                                       
               Prevents the "teleporting" by requiring local structure preservation                                                                                                     
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 These are physically-motivated priors. They encode the assumption that real objects in the world deform smoothly and locally — which is true for everything except explosions and      
 topology-changing events.                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Evaluating 4DGS — What Changes From Static                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 For static 3DGS, you hold out test cameras. For 4DGS, you have two independent test axes:                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Training cameras:  cameras 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6                                                                                                                                          
   Test cameras:      camera 7, 8               ← held out, never seen during training                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Training frames:   t = 0, 1, 2, ..., 90                                                                                                                                              
   Test frames:       t = 91, ..., 100          ← future timesteps, never seen                                                                                                          
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This gives you two evaluation settings:                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                                                             
 │ Setting                                            │ What It Tests                                                     │                                                             
 ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                             
 │ Novel View (test cameras, seen timesteps)          │ Can the model synthesize unseen viewpoints of motion it observed? │                                                             
 ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                             
 │ Novel Time (training cameras, future timesteps)    │ Can the model predict future states?                              │                                                             
 ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                             
 │ Novel View + Time (test cameras, future timesteps) │ Full generalization                                               │                                                             
 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 "Novel Time" is a form of video prediction — harder and less studied. Most 4DGS papers only evaluate novel view. But with our multi-camera dataset, we can evaluate all three.         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Current SOTA and Where the Field Is Going (2024-2025)                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   4D Methods Timeline:                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Oct 2023:  Deformable 3DGS (Yang et al.)    — deformation MLP                                                                                                                        
   Nov 2023:  4D Gaussian Splatting (Wu et al.) — 4D covariance                                                                                                                         
   Nov 2023:  Spacetime Gaussians (Li et al.)   — polynomial motion                                                                                                                     
   Dec 2023:  SC-GS                            — sparse control points + skinning                                                                                                       
   Feb 2024:  4DGaussians (Duan et al.)        — 4D SH for dynamic appearance                                                                                                           
   Mar 2024:  Gaussian-Flow                    — optical flow supervision                                                                                                               
   Jun 2024:  Dynamic 3D Gaussians (Luiten et al.) — physical consistency                                                                                                               
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Current practical recommendation (2025): For a multi-camera real scene:                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 1. Best quality: 4D Gaussian Splatting (Wu et al.) with multi-view input                                                                                                               
 2. Best speed + interpretability: Spacetime Gaussians                                                                                                                                  
 3. Best for learning: Deformable 3DGS — clearest codebase, most tutorials                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### The NLP Analogy for 4DGS                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Since this has been useful, here's how 4DGS maps to sequence modeling:                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ┌──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                                                                                    
 │ 4DGS Concept                 │ NLP Analogy                                                      │                                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                    
 │ Canonical Gaussians          │ Base vocabulary / pretrained weights                             │                                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                    
 │ Deformation network          │ Adapter / LoRA — small modification on top of base               │                                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                    
 │ Temporal positional encoding │ Sequence positional encoding                                     │                                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                    
 │ 4D covariance Σ_xt           │ Attention cross-temporal correlation                             │                                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                    
 │ Regularization losses        │ Weight decay / gradient clipping (prevent degenerate solutions)  │                                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                    
 │ Multi-view video training    │ Multi-document training with shared world model                  │                                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                    
 │ Novel time synthesis         │ Autoregressive text generation — predicting unseen future tokens │                                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                    
 │ Canonical space              │ The model's "world model" / factual knowledge                    │                                                                                    
 ├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                    
 │ Deformation at time t        │ The model's "context" given the current timestep                 │                                                                                    
 └──────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The deepest analogy: a canonical 3DGS + deformation network is structurally identical to a pretrained LLM + LoRA adapter. The canonical model encodes world knowledge (the scene's     
 static structure), and the lightweight adapter (deformation network) encodes the dynamic, context-dependent modification.                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Summary                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   The 4DGS design space in one diagram:                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   How to add time to 3DGS?                                                                                                                                                             
            │                                                                                                                                                                           
            ├── EXTERNAL: Deformation Field                                                                                                                                             
            │   "Time drives a function that warps the canonical scene"                                                                                                                 
            │   + Works for complex non-linear motion                                                                                                                                   
            │   - MLP is slow, reintroduces spectral bias                                                                                                                               
            │   - Can't handle topology changes                                                                                                                                         
            │                                                                                                                                                                           
            ├── INTERNAL: 4D Gaussian Covariance                                                                                                                                        
            │   "Time is just another dimension of the primitive"                                                                                                                       
            │   + Mathematically elegant, no extra network                                                                                                                              
            │   - Only linear motion per Gaussian                                                                                                                                       
            │   + Handles appearance/disappearance via temporal extent                                                                                                                  
            │                                                                                                                                                                           
            └── EXPLICIT: Motion Coefficients                                                                                                                                           
                "Each Gaussian has its own kinematic trajectory"                                                                                                                        
                + Fastest inference, physically interpretable                                                                                                                           
                + Handles appearance change via opacity trajectory
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
