 large spaces into manageable chunks. Research approaches like Block-NeRF train multiple overlapping NeRFs and blend them at boundaries, or use scene graphs to explicitly model        
 relationships between regions and objects.                                                                                                                                             
 8. The core tension: There's a fundamental tradeoff between scaling to large environments and maintaining reconstruction quality—pure single-model NeRFs struggle with this, which is  
 why practical solutions either add geometric constraints or break the scene into pieces.                                                                                               

 Great instinct. You've identified one of the most important unsolved practical problems in neural rendering. The honest answer is: it's genuinely hard, and different approaches       
 handle it in completely different ways.                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The Problems with Multi-Room Scenes                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 There are actually four separate problems stacked on top of each other.                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Problem 1 — The Overlap Problem (COLMAP / Pose Estimation)                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 For COLMAP to reconstruct camera poses, consecutive images need shared visible content. In a single room, this is fine — every adjacent image shares 60-80% of the scene. The trouble  
 happens at transitions:                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Living room → hallway → bedroom                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Images in living room:    lots of mutual overlap ✅                                                                                                                                  
   Images in hallway:        lots of mutual overlap ✅                                                                                                                                  
   The 2 images in doorway:  the ONLY bridge between them                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
           Living room         Hallway          Bedroom                                                                                                                                 
           [img1][img2][img3] [img4][img5] [img6][img7][img8]                                                                                                                           
                          ↑                ↑                                                                                                                                            
                     doorway 1         doorway 2                                                                                                                                        
                   (narrow overlap)  (narrow overlap)                                                                                                                                   
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 If you capture a home like a single continuous video, COLMAP can usually track through doorways — a hallway is still a physical 3D space with visible walls, floors, and door frames.  
 The feature tracks survive if the overlap is wide enough. But if the camera cuts between rooms (separate capture sessions, or a very narrow doorway), COLMAP loses the thread and the  
 reconstruction fragments into disconnected islands.                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 In practice: open-plan layouts and wide doorways are easy. A tiny bathroom with a narrow door viewed obliquely is much harder. A second floor accessed via stairs requires the         
 staircase to act as the connecting geometry.                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Problem 2 — Scale and Precision                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 3DGS and NeRF both operate in a normalized coordinate space. They work best when the scene fits roughly within a unit sphere or cube. A single room is maybe 4×5×3 meters — that's     
 fine. A full home might be 15×12×6 meters across two floors. At this scale:                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 - Floating point precision starts to matter. Small numerical errors that are invisible in a 5m scene produce visible artifacts in a 15m scene                                          
 - The Gaussian initialization is sparser because the COLMAP point cloud is spread across a much larger volume                                                                          
 - Adaptive density control has to allocate the same number of Gaussians across much more space                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Published papers show quality visibly degrades as scene scale increases. A single room at close range gets PSNR ~28-30dB. The same method applied to a full apartment typically gets   
 ~24-26dB.                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Problem 3 — Lighting Discontinuity                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is the least-discussed but arguably most important practical problem.                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Each room in a home has completely independent lighting:                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Living room:  south-facing windows, warm afternoon light, ceiling spots                                                                                                              
   Bedroom:      north-facing window, soft daylight, lamp on nightstand                                                                                                                 
   Bathroom:     artificial overhead light, no windows, cool white tone                                                                                                                 
   Kitchen:      direct sunlight through east window at 9am                                                                                                                             
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 In 3DGS, color is encoded as Spherical Harmonic coefficients — a view-dependent color function per Gaussian. SH can represent how a surface's appearance changes with viewing          
 direction, but it encodes one fixed illumination state. If the living room Gaussians are trained under afternoon sunlight and the bedroom Gaussians under artificial light, they exist 
 in completely different radiometric spaces. Rendering a consistent image across the boundary between them is physically incoherent.                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 NeRF in the Wild (Martin-Brualla et al., 2021) introduced per-image appearance embeddings to handle this — each training image gets a latent code representing its lighting            
 conditions. This partially addresses the problem but adds parameters and complexity.                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Problem 4 — Memory and Computation                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 A single-room 3DGS model uses 2-6 million Gaussians and ~700MB. A full home would naively require 20-40 million Gaussians and 4-8GB — pushing past typical VRAM limits, and making     
 training substantially slower. The depth-sort step (the back-to-front sort for correct alpha compositing) runs in O(N log N) so it gets meaningfully slower as N grows.                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 How the Industry Actually Handles This                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Matterport — The Market Leader                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Matterport doesn't use NeRF or 3DGS at all. They use a dedicated hardware camera (a structured-light depth sensor) that captures a precise depth map at each position. The camera sits 
 still, captures a panorama and depth map, the operator moves it to the next position, repeats every 1-2 meters.                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Capture positions in a home:                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
       [●]──[●]──[●]                                                                                                                                                                    
        │         │                                                                                                                                                                     
       [●]   ┌──[●]──[●]                                                                                                                                                                
        │    │         │                                                                                                                                                                
       [●]──[●]──[●]──[●]                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   Each [●] is a capture position with known relative geometry                                                                                                                          
   from the depth sensor + IMU + their proprietary alignment algorithm                                                                                                                  
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The reconstruction is room-by-room with explicit geometry (mesh + texture), stitched together with known metric scale from the depth sensor. The "3D tour" in Matterport is not        
 free-viewpoint rendering — it's discrete teleportation between capture positions with pre-rendered panoramas interpolated between them. It looks like free movement but you can only   
 actually stand where the tripod stood.                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This approach is robust, scalable, and produces consistent results — but requires specialized hardware, takes 45+ minutes per property, and costs ~$500/scan professionally.           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Luma AI — NeRF/3DGS Based                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Luma AI (2022-present) is the closest to what you'd imagine: capture a home with a smartphone, upload the video, get back a neural representation you can view from any angle.         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Their approach as far as is publicly documented:                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 1. Sequential COLMAP on the full video — tracking through the whole walkthrough including room transitions                                                                             
 2. Scene segmentation — automatically detect room boundaries based on geometry (walls, floors, ceilings)                                                                               
 3. Per-room models with overlap — train separate NeRF/3DGS models for each room but with shared overlap zones at doorways                                                              
 4. Blending at boundaries — when the viewpoint is near a doorway, blend between the adjacent room models                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The blending at boundaries is the hard part. If done naively you get a seam. Their approach appears to use the doorway region as a "transition zone" where both models contribute      
 weighted by distance from each room's center.                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### Block-NeRF (Waymo, 2022)                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is the most principled academic solution, designed for city-scale outdoor scenes but applicable to large indoor spaces.                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The idea: divide the scene into overlapping blocks. Train one NeRF per block. At inference time, determine which blocks are relevant for the current viewpoint and blend their         
 outputs.                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   Full scene divided into overlapping blocks:                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
       ┌────────┬────────┬────────┐                                                                                                                                                     
       │Block A │Block B │Block C │                                                                                                                                                     
       │        │   ←overlap→    │                                                                                                                                                      
       ├────────┼────────┼────────┤                                                                                                                                                     
       │Block D │Block E │Block F │                                                                                                                                                     
       │        │   ←overlap→    │                                                                                                                                                      
       └────────┴────────┴────────┘                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   At a viewpoint near the A-B boundary:                                                                                                                                                
     final_color = w_A × render(Block A, viewpoint) + w_B × render(Block B, viewpoint)                                                                                                  
     where w_A + w_B = 1, based on proximity                                                                                                                                            
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Each block is trained independently, so you can train them in parallel. The overlap zones provide consistency. The main problems: blending can produce ghosting at boundaries, and you 
 need to handle appearance consistency (lighting) across blocks.                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ### City Gaussian (2024) and Scaffold-GS                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 These are 3DGS extensions specifically designed for large scenes:                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Scaffold-GS (2024): Instead of placing Gaussians independently, anchors them to a sparse voxel scaffold. The scaffold provides spatial regularity, dramatically reduces Gaussian       
 count, and gives the optimization a structured prior that helps at large scales.                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 City Gaussian (2024): Partitions the city/large scene into cells, trains local Gaussian models per cell with overlap, uses level-of-detail (LOD) — coarser Gaussians for distant       
 content, finer for close content. Demonstrated rendering of entire city blocks from street-level captures.                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The Emerging Practical Answer for Real Estate                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The architecture that makes most sense for production real estate today is a hybrid:                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
   CAPTURE:                                                                                                                                                                             
     Walk through home continuously with iPhone/high-quality phone                                                                                                                      
     One continuous video, 5-10 minutes, 30fps                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   POSE ESTIMATION:                                                                                                                                                                     
     Run COLMAP or MASt3R on the full video                                                                                                                                             
     Sequential matching follows camera through doorways                                                                                                                                
     If rooms disconnect: treat each connected component as a zone                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   PER-ZONE TRAINING:                                                                                                                                                                   
     Identify zones (rooms) by clustering camera positions                                                                                                                              
     Train one 3DGS model per zone                                                                                                                                                      
     Include a ~1 meter overlap buffer at zone boundaries                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   VIEWER:                                                                                                                                                                              
     As the virtual camera moves, determine the current zone                                                                                                                            
     Render using that zone's model                                                                                                                                                     
     At zone boundaries: crossfade between adjacent models                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
   LIGHTING:                                                                                                                                                                            
     Per-image appearance embeddings during training                                                                                                                                    
     Each zone has its own "canonical" lighting state                                                                                                                                   
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 This is not a solved problem — there's no off-the-shelf package that does all of this cleanly. The companies doing it well (Luma, Polycam, Matterport's newer NeRF-based experiments)  
 are treating the seaming and blending as proprietary engineering.                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The Deeper Question You're Implying                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 What you're really asking is: where does "one scene" end and "multiple scenes" begin?                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The answer in 3DGS/NeRF terms is: a scene is the connected component of camera poses that share sufficient visual overlap for pose estimation to work. Anything connected is one       
 scene. Anything disconnected is multiple scenes.                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 For a home: if you walk continuously with a camera and every doorway is wide enough for COLMAP to track through, the entire home is one scene in principle. Whether it should be       
 trained as one model or several depends on scale, lighting variation, and available VRAM. Current best practice for homes over ~80 sqm is per-room models with explicit boundary       
 handling.                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 For comparison: the Mip-NeRF 360 dataset's "garden" scene covers roughly 20×15 meters of outdoor space as a single model — larger than many apartments. Indoor scenes with controlled  
 lighting can be handled at similar scales. The problem is specifically the lighting discontinuity between rooms, which outdoor scenes don't have.

 So the core issue is that each framework needs a different version of the same package - gaussian-splatting requires the standard version while Deformable-3DGS needs the one with the 
 means2D_densify parameter for improved gradient computation. The typical workarounds are using separate environments, reinstalling between runs, or finding a way to import both with  
 different paths.                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Since the training runs as subprocesses, I could reinstall the correct rasterizer before each training job, but the cleanest approach for this project would be to stick with a single 
 conda environment and just use whichever rasterizer each training script needs - the standard one for static 3DGS and the depth version for dynamic 4DGS training.                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Now I'm mapping out the actual scripts I need to write: the static training script will rebuild the sparse directory with proper image naming, set up the test split, and run the      
 gaussian-splatting trainer; then an evaluation script to compute metrics on the rendered outputs; and a visualization script to inspect the learned gaussians.                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 For the dynamic phase, I'll need to reinstall the different rasterizer and patch the camera loading to match our naming convention before running the deformable trainer.              
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 I'm also planning ablation and comparison scripts to test different hyperparameters and aggregate results across experiments.

 OK so llffhold is hardcoded at 8 (or 4 if "360" in path, but actually looking at the code again, it only defaults to 8 at the function definition). The test.txt path is taken when    
 llffhold is falsy (0 or None), which is determined inside the function not from args. There's no command-line argument for llffhold.                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 BUT looking at the code again:                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```python                                                                                                                                                                              
   if eval:                                                                                                                                                                             
       if "360" in path:                                                                                                                                                                
           llffhold = 8                                                                                                                                                                 
       if llffhold:                                                                                                                                                                     
           ...use llffhold...                                                                                                                                                           
       else:                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 ```                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 Wait, llffhold=8 is the function default. Inside the function, when eval is true and "360" is in the path, it reassigns llffhold to 8, then checks if that value is truthy. The        
 test.txt path only gets used when llffhold is 0 or None, which can't happen from the command line since there's no way to pass that parameter. To actually trigger the test.txt        
 branch, I'd need to explicitly pass llffhold=0 as a function argument.                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 But actually, the cleaner solution is to skip the --eval flag entirely during training. I'll just put the three training images in the images folder, train without evaluation, then   
 use a separate script to render from the fourth camera's viewpoint. This way the model only sees three cameras during training and never encounters the fourth one. For rendering, I   
 can add the fourth camera to the dataset without marking it as a training image, then use the render script to generate views from that pose.                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The simplest approach is to train without --eval on the first three cameras, then load the trained model directly in Python and render from the fourth camera's pose using the         
 rasterizer myself. This gives me complete control over the evaluation process.

 Training 3DGS with only 3-4 images will inherently limit quality due to sparse multi-view constraints, so the model will likely overfit while struggling with novel views. Rather than 
 patching the original Deformable-3DGS code, I'll work with the existing image naming convention by mapping our dynamic image files to a format the code expects, tracking which camera 
 corresponds to each numbered file.                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 The issue is that the code tries to parse image names as pure integers to compute frame indices, but our naming scheme includes camera and frame information. I'm adding a fallback    
 that uses regex to extract the frame number from our naming pattern and normalizes it against the maximum frame count across all images.
